relations.subject: capella:bucket
relations.evidence: If you're using a free tier operational cluster, you cannot create a bucket with advanced settings. Free tier clusters can create buckets only with the memory and disk bucket type, and the Magma 128 vBucket storage backend option.

relations.subject: capella:bucket
relations.evidence: When using Couchbase Server 8.0 or later, the default storage backend is Magma, which needs 100 MiB with 128 vBuckets or 1 GiB with 1024 vBuckets.

relations.subject: capella:bucket
relations.evidence: **Couchstore**: Best if your dataset is small and fits into memory. Choose this for datasets that require a minimum of 100 MiB memory.

notable_absence.finding: No Enterprise/Community edition badges anywhere on this page (known recurring anomaly, absent here as on every other Capella page checked this batch) - the only gating axes present are capella-role:* (project-scope, disjunctive) and billing plan tier (Free Tier's advanced-settings restriction), never edition. Note the page DOES cite bare server-version strings twice ('Couchbase Server 8.0 and later', 'Couchbase Server 7.6 or earlier') for XDCR/storage-backend defaults - the OTHER known recurring anomaly, present here as expected.

cross_component_finding: Restates the exact same disjunctive Project Owner/Cluster Manager gate seen on allow-ip-address.md and manage-database-users.md, but this page ALSO explicitly states the Organization Owner->Project Owner impliesRole shortcut inline ('If you have the Organization Owner role, you have Project Owner access') - the same mechanic manage-database-users.md's Prerequisites section omitted. Net: across this batch's 3 access-gated pages (allow-ip-address, manage-database-users, manage-buckets/scopes-collections), the disjunctive project-scope pair (Project Owner, Cluster Manager) is completely consistent; only the presence/absence of the inline Organization Owner shortcut note varies page to page, a minor but real documentation inconsistency worth flagging rather than a role-catalog problem.
cross_product_finding: The Magma/Couchstore storage-backend choice, vBucket count (128 vs 1024), XDCR cross-storage-backend support gated by 'Couchbase Server 8.0 and later', and durability levels are all identical concepts/vocabulary to server/'s own bucket documentation (explicitly linked via 'For more information... in the Couchbase Server documentation' cross-references throughout) - Capella's bucket configuration surface is a UI wrapper around server/'s own bucket model, not a parallel Capella-specific one, unlike the role/privilege/credential layer covered in cluster-rbac.json.
